external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card-processor
external_entities.description: Third party card processor that settles payments and POSTs a webhook back
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party. After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API

processes.name: storefront-api
processes.description: Node service running on Cloud Run exposing the storefront API to the internet
processes.source_excerpt: storefront-api, a Node service running on Cloud Run. It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

processes.name: order-service
processes.description: Python worker in our core network handling orders
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network; it is not exposed outside.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: PostgreSQL database storing orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt-archive
data_stores.description: Cloud Storage bucket storing order receipts
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: browse-and-order
data_flows.description: Shoppers browse storefront and place orders, signing in with email and password
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API... Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: submit-order
data_flows.description: Storefront API calls the order service over gRPC when a shopper submits an order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC. There is no auth on that gRPC call

data_flows.name: read-write-orders
data_flows.description: Order service reads and writes to orders-db using an application account
data_flows.source_excerpt: that the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write. The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: application account password from environment variable

data_flows.name: write-receipt
data_flows.description: Order service writes a receipt to the receipt archive bucket
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive. That is on TLS with the order service's own service account

data_flows.name: payment-webhook
data_flows.description: Card processor posts a webhook back to the storefront API after payment settlement
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid. I would have to check how that callback is authenticated.
data_flows.notes: Speaker notes: 'I would have to check how that callback is authenticated.'
